passages.text: This is Solomon’s Song of Songs.
passages.sermon: Solomon wrote this song.\r\nThis song is called the Song of Songs.\r\nThis song is the greatest of all songs.

passages.text: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is more delightful than wine.
passages.sermon:
This is Solomon’s Song of Songs.
A woman speaks.
She desires her beloved.
She says, “Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth.”
She explains her desire.
She says, “Your love is more delightful than wine.”
passages.original: יִשָּׁקֵ֙נִי֙ מִנְּשִׁיק֣וֹת פִּ֔יהוּ כִּֽי־ טוֹבִ֥ים דֹּדֶ֖יךָ מִיָּֽיִן׃

passages.text: The fragrance of your perfume is pleasing; your name is like perfume poured out. No wonder the maidens adore you.
passages.sermon:
This is Solomon’s Song of Songs.
Your perfume smells very good.
Your name is like perfume poured out.
The maidens love you.
passages.original: לְרֵ֙יחַ֙ שְׁמָנֶ֣יךָ טוֹבִ֔ים שֶׁ֖מֶן תּוּרַ֣ק שְׁמֶ֑ךָ עַל־ כֵּ֖ן עֲלָמ֥וֹת אֲהֵבֽוּךָ׃

passages.text: Take me away with you—let us hurry! May the king bring me to his chambers. We will rejoice and delight in you; we will praise your love more than wine. It is only right that they adore you.
passages.sermon:
A woman speaks to her beloved.
She desires to be close to him.
She says, "Draw me after you."
She wants to follow him quickly.
She says, "Let us run together."
She calls him king.
She asks the king to bring her into his rooms.
She promises joy in his presence.
She says, "We will rejoice in you."
She says, "We will be glad with you."
She promises to praise his love.
She says, "We will remember your love more than wine."
She says, "It is right that others love you."
passages.original: מָשְׁכֵ֖נִי אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ נָּר֑וּצָה הֱבִיאַ֨נִי הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ חֲדָרָ֗יו נָגִ֤ילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה֙ בָּ֔ךְ נַזְכִּ֤ירָה דֹדֶ֙יךָ֙ מִיַּ֔יִן מֵישָׁרִ֖ים אֲהֵבֽוּךָ׃ס

passages.text: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a woman.
She speaks to the daughters of Jerusalem.
She says, “I am dark.”
She also says, “I am lovely.”
She compares herself to the tents of Kedar.
She also compares herself to the curtains of Solomon.
passages.original: שְׁחוֹרָ֤ה אֲנִי֙ וְֽנָאוָ֔ה בְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כְּאָהֳלֵ֣י קֵדָ֔ר כִּירִיע֖וֹת שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

passages.text: Do not stare because I am dark, for the sun has gazed upon me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; they made me a keeper of the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have neglected.
passages.sermon:
I am a woman who is dark in appearance.
The sun has made my skin dark.
Do not stare at me because I am dark.
My mother’s sons became angry with me.
They made me watch over the vineyards.
I had to care for their vineyards.
I did not care for my own vineyard.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּרְא֙וּנִי֙ שֶׁאֲנִ֣י שְׁחַרְחֹ֔רֶת שֶׁשֱּׁזָפַ֖תְנִי הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י נִֽחֲרוּ־ בִ֗י שָׂמֻ֙נִי֙ נֹטֵרָ֣ה אֶת־ הַכְּרָמִ֔ים כַּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י לֹ֥א נָטָֽרְתִּי׃

passages.text: Tell me, O one I love, where do you pasture your sheep? Where do you rest them at midday? Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your companions?
passages.sermon:
The woman speaks to the one she loves.
She asks him a question.
She says, "Tell me where you pasture your sheep."
She also asks, "Where do you rest your sheep at midday?"
She wants to know his location.
She asks another question.
She says, "Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your companions?"
She does not want to wander among others, hidden and uncertain.
She wants to be with the one she loves.
passages.original: הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י שֶׁ֤אָהֲבָה֙ נַפְשִׁ֔י אֵיכָ֣ה תִרְעֶ֔ה אֵיכָ֖ה תַּרְבִּ֣יץ בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם שַׁלָּמָ֤ה אֶֽהְיֶה֙ כְּעֹ֣טְיָ֔ה עַ֖ל עֶדְרֵ֥י חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: If you do not know, O fairest of women, follow the tracks of the flock, and graze your young goats near the tents of the shepherds.
passages.sermon:
You are the most beautiful among women.
If you do not know where to go,
Follow the tracks of the sheep.
Take your young goats with you.
Let them graze near the tents of the shepherds.
passages.original: אִם־ לֹ֤א תֵדְעִי֙ לָ֔ךְ הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים צְֽאִי־ לָ֞ךְ בְּעִקְבֵ֣י הַצֹּ֗אן וּרְעִי֙ אֶת־ גְּדִיֹּתַ֔יִךְ עַ֖ל מִשְׁכְּנ֥וֹת הָרֹעִֽים׃ס

passages.text: I compare you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses his beloved.
He calls her "my darling."
He compares her to a mare.
This mare stands among Pharaoh’s chariots.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh’s chariots were strong and impressive.
A mare among these chariots is beautiful and noble.
The speaker says his beloved is like this mare.
She is beautiful and noble among others.

passages.text: Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses a woman who is called the fairest among women.
The speaker describes her appearance.
Her cheeks look beautiful.
Ornaments decorate her cheeks.
Her neck looks beautiful.
Strings of jewels decorate her neck.

passages.text: We will make you ornaments of gold, studded with beads of silver.
passages.sermon:
We will make ornaments for you.
These ornaments will be gold.
We will add beads of silver to them.
The ornaments will be beautiful and valuable.
passages.original: תּוֹרֵ֤י זָהָב֙ נַעֲשֶׂה־ לָּ֔ךְ עִ֖ם נְקֻדּ֥וֹת הַכָּֽסֶף׃

passages.text: While the king was at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
passages.sermon:
The king sat at his table.
I wore perfume.
My perfume gave a pleasant smell.
The fragrance spread while the king was present.
passages.original: עַד־ שֶׁ֤הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בִּמְסִבּ֔וֹ נִרְדִּ֖י נָתַ֥ן רֵיחֽוֹ׃

passages.text: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.
passages.sermon:
My beloved is precious to me.
He is like a sachet of myrrh.
This sachet rests between my breasts.
My beloved stays close to my heart.
He brings fragrance and comfort.
passages.original: צְר֨וֹר הַמֹּ֤ר׀ דּוֹדִי֙ לִ֔י בֵּ֥ין שָׁדַ֖י יָלִֽין׃

passages.text: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi.
passages.sermon:
My beloved is precious to me.
My beloved is like a cluster of henna blossoms.
These blossoms grow in the vineyards of En-gedi.
En-gedi is a place known for its beauty and gardens.
Henna blossoms are fragrant and lovely.
My beloved brings beauty and delight, like these blossoms.
passages.original: אֶשְׁכֹּ֨ל הַכֹּ֤פֶר׀ דּוֹדִי֙ לִ֔י בְּכַרְמֵ֖י עֵ֥ין גֶּֽדִי׃ס

passages.text: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves.
passages.sermon: My darling, you are beautiful.\r\nYou are very beautiful.\r\nYour eyes are like doves.
passages.original: הִנָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י הִנָּ֥ךְ יָפָ֖ה עֵינַ֥יִךְ יוֹנִֽים׃

passages.text: How handsome you are, my beloved! Oh, how delightful! The soft grass is our bed.
passages.sermon: My beloved is handsome.\r\nMy beloved is delightful.\r\nOur bed is fresh grass.
passages.original: הִנְּךָ֨ יָפֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ אַ֣ף נָעִ֔ים אַף־ עַרְשֵׂ֖נוּ רַעֲנָנָֽה׃

passages.text: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are fragrant firs.
passages.sermon:
Our house has strong beams.
The beams are made of cedar wood.
Our house has rafters.
The rafters are made of fir trees.
The fir trees are fragrant.
